name: MCA insular segment (M2)
synonyms: M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery
insular branches of the middle cerebral artery
function: The insular segment of the middle cerebral artery: after leaving the Sylvian cistern the M1 trunk divides at the limen insulae into two (sometimes three) trunks that run across the insula in the Sylvian fissure â€” the M2 segment â€” before turning at the circular sulcus onto the opercular surface as the M3 segments. The M2 branches are the intermediate vessels of the MCA tree: they give off the small insular perforators to the claustrum, external capsule and extreme capsule, and they are the vessels that must be preserved when the Sylvian fissure is split. Because they lie on the insula, an occlusion of a single M2 branch produces a partial MCA syndrome â€” a division infarct â€” rather than the complete territory deficit.

Small insular perforators to the claustrum, external and extreme capsules
